extracted.intended_audience: unemployed younger sons of the nobility; gentlemen considering genteel professions/auctioneering
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and prescriptive standards for gentlemen who would adopt auctioneering as a respectable, lucrative profession — describing required qualities, scope of goods to handle, manners, and professional conduct. Framed as guidance to aristocratic younger sons seeking a new calling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of the auctioneer's pulpit for a gentleman
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer's pulpit is 'the peculiar place where a man of social refinement, of elegant wit, of polite perceptions, can bring his wit, his eloquence, his taste, and his experience of life, most delightfully into play.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument that auctioneering (properly done) allows a cultivated gentleman to exercise higher qualities than many other professions; contrasted with the legal bar where technical knowledge often outweighs social polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate selection of goods (focus on 'things of taste')
rubrics_metrics.description: A gentleman-auctioneer should not be called upon to sell lowly/commercial items (pigs, ploughs, schooners, beer-barrels); 'all articles properly called of taste should be put under his charge.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of suitable goods: pictures, china, jewelry, gold-headed canes, valuable arms, picturesque antiquities, lighter literature, and fashionable bric-à-brac. Avoid sales of coarse or purely utilitarian trade goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refined promotion; avoid vulgar advertisement and 'Bartholomew-fair advocacy'
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejects the noisy, hoarse, trumpeting style of popular auctioneers: 'Bartholomew-fair advocacy...hoarse yelling, twenty-four drums' which drives refined buyers away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns: extravagant trumpetings, swaggering quackery in advertisements, vulgar trumpeting or bluster. Instead adopt a refined, tasteful manner of attracting the genteel public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad cultural knowledge and taste in art and literature
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'must have a good knowledge of the history and language of all nations; not the knowledge of the mere critical scholar, but of the lively and elegant man of the world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be able to speak intelligibly and attractively about pictures, authors, bindings, and the provenance/history of objects to inspire confidence and purchases among a cultivated clientele.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and refusal to misrepresent goods
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer 'must not sacrifice his honesty...nor tell fibs about himself or them' — he should preserve a character of sincerity and not falsely advertise items (e.g., pass a copy of Raffaelle for an original).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duty both to clients who consign goods and to the public as his client; calibrated praise is acceptable but gross falsification or over-valuation is intolerable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polished social tact and appropriate rhetoric
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'must have the confidence of your society...to plant a happy mot in a graceful manner, to appeal to my lord or the duchess in such a modest, easy, pleasant way' and 'know where a joke is in place, and how far a compliment may go.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wit, modesty, and tact in address. Avoid offending or embarrassing patrons; tailor rhetoric to a genteel audience to attract them rather than repel them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of pomposity and grandiose titles
rubrics_metrics.description: He should avoid pompous self-styling: not calling his room a 'study' (prefer 'private room' or 'office') and not styling himself an 'advocate' when he is an auctioneer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain modest presentation and truthful titles — ostentation or exaggerated titles are vulgar and counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreeable personal presentation and social standing
rubrics_metrics.description: His person should be so agreeable 'that it must be a pleasure for ladies to behold and tailors to dress it' and he should move in the best society so that people will flock to his pulpit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dress, deportment, and connections matter: a genteel appearance and membership in or familiarity with fashionable society will attract the desired clientele.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine enthusiasm and sincere feeling for objects
rubrics_metrics.description: He should be 'an artist above all, adoring his profession; and adoring it, what must he not know?...He must feel every one of these things in his heart. Nor must he affect these things; he must feel them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic passion for the objects and the profession enables persuasive, convincing salesmanship; affectation is detectable and harms credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate specialization and limits of practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that the genteel auctioneer not 'meddle with heavy antiquarian and philological works' and to concentrate on lighter literature and tasteful objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know your niche and do not overreach into technical specialties better handled by antiquarians or philologists; specialization increases credibility with target clientele.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct pronunciation and measured praise in speech
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'will not commit the gross blunders of pronunciation that untravelled Englishmen perpetrate; he will not degrade his subject by coarse eulogy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speak grammatically and elegantly; avoid coarse or indiscriminate laudation. Calibration of praise is important — know when to praise and when restraint preserves trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key character traits: truth, imagination, wit, benevolence
rubrics_metrics.description: An auctioneer 'should have the organ of truth large; of imagination and comparison, considerable; of wit, great; of benevolence, excessively large.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These personal faculties are cited as essential ingredients of success — truth for integrity, imagination for lively description, wit for charm, benevolence for goodwill toward clients and public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-mindedness: treat the public as a client
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'is not merely the advocate of the person who employs him, but that the public is his client too, who honors him and confides in him.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility extends beyond the consignor; maintain fairness and cultivate public trust because the auctioneer serves and depends upon the public market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptability: assume characters to suit audience
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'must be every one of the characters to whom he addresses himself' — a genteel Goethe or Shakespeare, a fashionable world-spirit, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to shift tone and persona to resonate with different segments of a refined audience enhances persuasive effect and broadens appeal.
